name: Nikolai Bukharin
role: Russian Bolshevik theorist and Soviet leader (1888-1938), editor of Pravda, executed in the Great Purge
summary: Bukharin, Bolshevik economist and editor of Pravda, co-wrote The ABC of Communism, defending the proletarian dictatorship, terror in extreme cases, nationalisation, planned production for use and the eventual abolition of money, the State and religion; in the 1920s he backed the NEP alliance with the peasantry.

Read by theme in The ABC of Communism (1920, with Preobrazhensky: chapters 3-8, 11-12, 15), Programme of the World Revolution ch. 12 (1918) and Soviets or Parliament (1919), all from the Marxists Internet Archive corpus. His views changed: the 1919-20 war-communism ABC was followed from 1921 by the NEP position he defended until 1929, which is his mature view; where the two differ (money, markets, the peasant, planning) the NEP texts decide the answer and the ABC remains as history in the rationale. The NEP texts read: his July 1921 essay, 'The Economic Structure of Soviet Russia' (1922), the 1923 smychka article, The Tasks of the Russian Communist Party (January 1926), the December 1926 Comintern speech and the 1928 article 'Observations of an Economist' (the Notes of an Economist theme; an English transcription). 'The Road to Socialism and the Worker-Peasant Alliance' (1925) and the 'enrich yourselves' speech were not found as open texts (see notFound). His 1938 last plea at the Moscow trial is a coerced confession, not a position, and is not used. Also read by keyword and settling no further answers: Imperialism and World Economy (1917) and Imperialism and the Accumulation of Capital, Historical Materialism, Economic Theory of the Leisure Class (its free-trade and protectionism passages concern the history of economic theory), the Comintern speeches of 1922-27, the 1920-21 NEP essays and the 1938 trial; the 1923 smychka article and the 1922 draft programme, 1933 Marx's Teaching chapter 4 are cited above.
